result.title: Backward Conformal Prediction under Covariate Shift
result.summary: Backward conformal prediction (BCP) fixes the size of a prediction set and estimates its miscoverage, but assumes calibration and test data are exchangeable. We extend BCP to covariate shift through importance weighting, preserving its guarantees when the density ratio is known. We show that BCP's tight miscoverage report depends only on the relative weight assigned to missed calibration examples, explaining why a better domain classifier can sometimes produce a worse estimate. Motivated by the fact that BCP depends only on nonconformity scores, we propose estimating density ratios on sorted score vectors rather than high-dimensional inputs. We prove that this approach recovers the same report asymptotically under an interpretable condition and characterize the resulting bias otherwise. Experiments with simulated and benchmark distribution shifts show that the proposed method improves BCP's miscoverage estimates, while score-based weighting consistently yields more accurate estimates than embedding-based weighting.

AI.brief_summary: 将 backward conformal prediction（固定预测集大小、估计未覆盖率）扩展到协变量偏移：用重要性加权维持保证，并提出在排序后的非一致性分数向量上估计密度比，证明可渐近恢复同一报告并刻画偏差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「固定预算下估计可靠性」与未覆盖率控制框架，可能与 LVR 的 STOP 决策及 latent 推理评估在分布偏移下的可信度相关；「报告只取决于漏检校准样本的相对权重」这一结论可供核查加权或缓存结构对估计的影响，属推测性借鉴。
